maya: heads up — cert-rotator started failing unseal in eu-west around 04:13 UTC, lots of downstream mTLS handshakes dropping.
owen: was there an RBAC prune job around then?
chris_s: yes, infra scheduled an RBAC prune at 04:10, but I thought it was in dry-run mode.
maya: logs from proxy (redacted):
```
2026-03-24T04:13:17Z proxy-eu-3 WARN mTLS: cert unseal failure: kms:Decrypt AccessDenied for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123:key/xyz
stack: keystore.unseal -> rotator.apply -> proxy.start
```
lee: keystore API returned 403 with body: {"code":"forbidden","detail":"permission denied: kms:Decrypt"} across ~18 proxies.
oncall: what is scope — all services or just rotator consumers?
own: mainly rotator and proxy clusters in eu-west, some ingress nodes retried and served stale certs but latency spiked. No customer data exposure.
maya: audit shows RBAC prune run by `infra-batch` at 04:09 removed `keystore.decrypt` binding from group `svc-proxy-eu`.
ochris_s: ok that matches. Why did dry-run not run?
own: the prune invocation omitted `--dry-run` because the job wrapper had an env var flip during a pipeline update.
lee: immediate fixes: A) emergency binding: add `keystore.decrypt` back to `svc-proxy-eu` (fast), B) reboot proxies to pick up new token (takes minutes), C) enable cross-account KMS fallback to central decrypter (slower). Which do we want?
maya: do A now. I'll request emergency approval.
infra-bot: emergency change request opened by maya: https://git.internal/infra/rbac/pull/422 — approvers: infra-ops.
oncall: infra-ops approve?
infra-bot: infra-ops approved at 04:17 UTC.
own: binding applied 04:18:05, proxies started succeeding decrypt at 04:18:30. Handshake error rate returned to baseline by 04:21.
maya: tagging logs with incident id `inc-1719956789` for SOC bundle.
soc-bot: SOC notified and requested full CloudTrail export for 04:00-05:00 UTC.
chris_s: root cause hypothesis: prune script is too eager and our pipeline change accidentally toggled dry-run.
lee: follow-ups: 1) enforce dry-run by default with explicit override bit, 2) add pre-prune canary that performs kms:Decrypt with a synthetic key per region and aborts if any fail, 3) add CI guard that prevents pipeline flips without two approvers, 4) expose a protected RBAC allowlist that cannot be removed by prune jobs (keystore, cert-rotator, proxy groups).
own: monitoring change: create alert when >15% of proxies in a region report kms decrypt 403s within 3m. Example detection: `sum(rate(kms_decrypt_denied_total{region="eu-west"}[3m])) / sum(up{job="proxy",region="eu-west"}) > 0.15`
maya: also add runbook steps for auto-escalation: auto-open revert PR + page infra-ops if threshold crossed.
chris_s: I'll draft the revert automation and a unit test that runs a simulated mTLS handshake using the service account token before prune proceeds.
lee: compliance note: we've got an audit trail and no keys were exported. SOC will review the audit bundle; we should keep logs for 60 days for this incident.
infra-bot: scheduled job `rbac-prune` paused until 2026-03-27T00:00Z.
oncall: filing incident for RCA and action items: https://pm.internal/incidents/INC-2026-03145 assigned to @chris_s (RBAC pipeline) and @lee (rotator hardening).
maya: TL;DR: accidental non-dry-run RBAC prune removed kms:Decrypt from proxy group in eu-west, caused rotator/proxy mTLS failures; mitigation = emergency binding revert; actions = dry-run default, pre-prune canary, allowlist, monitoring + SOC export.
lee: any objections to adding a short-lived allowlist exemption for keystore-related groups?
own: none, but treat exemptions narrowly and add periodic review.
chris_s: will post the proposed CI change and canary script in #eng-ml for review.
oncall: closing unless we see reoccurrence — reopen thread if new errors surface. :white_check_mark:
